content: Item 2 of the one-at-a-time order (supervisor 16:5x, user: 'why is A's geometry not better than the original'): row 4's session-end refinement supervised by the layer's frame archive (every stored 5 Hz frame of the session, T1-authorised) instead of GaME's keyframes only. Offline validation on real_row4v2/checkpoint_a (session A, no memory, so G5 plays no part); no mapping run. Starts only after item 1 (first-echo readout) has its conclusion and this review is approved.
Only row 4 (the method). Rows 1 and 3 stay GaME as published: refinement over keyframes (GaME run.py:36-37 optimize_model(refinement_iters, refinement=True)).

active_window.cpp:176-182 @192c1cf: every processed frame is offered to the session's FrameArchive with the rejected pixels (dynamic semantics, motion and dynamic clusters) removed; session_refusion.cpp step 2 (891-929) re-fuses the present from those frames (present_tsdf.cpp PresentTsdf::integrate over frame_archive.cpp frames). The present is estimated from all the session's frames, not a keyframe subset.

The session-end re-estimation of the present = GaME's refinement (F1, game.py finish_session) whose supervision set becomes the archive: each archived frame t supervises only the Gaussians alive at t (T1, backends/game/t1.py alive_at), its dynamic pixels (people + D1 motion: frames.dynamic_mask) excluded from the loss as GaME excludes occlusion-masked pixels; colour + depth loss, weights, iterations (refinement_iters 30000, flat.yaml:12), densification schedule (flat.yaml:25-27) unchanged.

Khronos eq. 5: the measurement of time t is generated by the scene of time t. An archived frame at t sees the scene at t; rendering it with the Gaussians alive at t (state births from the registry, background from -infinity, ends from the layer) is exactly 'the map of time t'. The archive frames are measurements of the same sensor and poses (ORB-SLAM3, the same as the keyframes); nothing in the archive is a new kind of input.

(a) the stored frames' poses are as good as the keyframes' (same trajectory source); (b) 30000 iterations over ~660 frames (each frame ~45 samples) converge as GaME's 30000 over 209 keyframes (~143 each) -- checked by the prediction, not assumed silently; (c) RGB at GaME's input resolution is loaded from the dataset for the archived stamps (the layer store keeps ranges and identity codes, not colour).

Archive = the layer's EvidenceStore frames: every 6th input frame (5 Hz, run.json layer_frame_step 6); the TSDF archive takes every processed frame. Same sensor frames at a lower rate, all within the session; the 5 Hz set already gives ~3x the keyframes (A: ~660 vs 209). Whether 5 Hz vs every frame matters is not tested here (stated, not assumed equal).

GaME trains only pixels with measured depth (C4) at its input resolution (pixel_step 2: 960x540); the archive frames are loaded at the same resolution and step. Dynamic mask: frames.dynamic_mask (people = semantic 12 without identity, + D1 motion pixels) -- the same mask the layer and every backend already use.
No new number. Iterations, learning rates, loss weights, densification: GaME flat.yaml unchanged. Keyframe selection thresholds are not used for the archive (every stored frame).

G1@5 P/R/F1 of session A, median-depth TSDF export (eval/tsdf_export.py, the same views, voxel 2 cm, sdf_trunc 5 voxels, measured-depth pixels) and the error decomposition (eval/g1_decompose.py: precision change / behind / in front / lateral; recall change / unobserved / observed-but-missing), against row 3 A and v2 A (both already measured with the same tools).

Open decision, stated before running: the median export fuses the rendered depth of the KEYFRAMES; with keyframe views the export can only show surface the keyframes see, which caps recall whatever the map holds. For this offline check: report both (a) keyframe views (as rows 1/3/v2 today, identical protocol) and (b) archive views, applied to row 3 A and v2 A as well (row 3 / v2 checkpoints + the same archive stamps), so every row is compared under the same views. The protocol for later runs is decided from this check, for all rows alike.
The snapshot readout is not involved (G1 is read from the median export). E1's 0.25 / 5% are not on this path.

analysis/item2/: the refined checkpoint (checkpoint_a_archive.pt), the exports (keyframe views and archive views) of row 3 A, v2 A and the refined A, G1 jsons, decomposition jsons, the log; the input checkpoint is read only.

Same code commit, real A: (1) 300 iterations over the archive, export with both views, G1 + decomposition, to check the chain end to end (frame loading, masks, T1 alive per frame, export); (2) then the full 30000. Synthetic: the same loader on synthetic A (stamps, resolution, pixel offset 0.5) for 300 iterations only, to catch dataset-specific errors before any later row uses it. Session boundaries: A only here (no memory); B/C are covered when row 4 is re-run, with its own review.

GPU: no other GaME job (queue empty since 16:38); refinement on 1.74M Gaussians: VRAM ~10-13 GB (row 4 refinement peaked 14.7 GB with the layer state loaded; offline without the layer: lower); one job at a time under side_gate --gpu. RAM: checkpoint_a 4.3 GB + ~660 frames of colour+depth at 960x540 (~4 GB) on the CPU, loaded on demand per iteration if needed. Failure: exit code and log; an OOM is not retried blindly -- frames move to on-demand loading first.

If the keyframe subset limits recall: G1@5 R of A (median export, archive views) rises clearly above v2 A's 90.84 (>= +2 pp) and 'observed but missing' falls below 4.74%; P stays >= 95.0 (v2 A 95.37). With keyframe views the gain is smaller (the views cap it).

R rises by < 1 pp under archive views, or P drops by > 0.5 pp, or 'in front' rises above 3% (the regression's signature): then the keyframe subset is not what limits A's recall, and item 2 is not merged.
If confirmed: implement in the mapping run (finish_session over the archive), write the review for the real row 4 re-run with it, run that row alone, evaluate, then the next item.
